title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
prompt:
Given an unsorted array, return the length of the longest run of **consecutive integers** (e.g. 1,2,3,4). Must run in O(n) — so no sorting.

**Example**: `[100,4,200,1,3,2]` → `4` (the run 1,2,3,4).

Dump everything into a HashSet, then only start counting from numbers that are the START of a run.
hints: Put all numbers in a HashSet for O(1) membership.
A number `x` starts a run only if `x - 1` is NOT in the set — otherwise skip it (something earlier will count it).
From each run-start, walk `x+1, x+2, …` while they're in the set; that guarantees O(n) total work.

solution.explanation: O(n). The `x - 1` guard is what keeps it linear: each run is walked exactly once, from its smallest element, so the inner while-loop across the whole algorithm does at most n steps total — not O(n) per element.
